rules.rationale: Hydrogen-bond donors (OH, NH) add polar surface area, raising aqueous solubility.
Moderate donor count still adds polar surface, though less than high-donor molecules.
Short SMILES implies compact molecular size, which raises solubility by reducing hydrophobic surface.
Lack of hydrogen bonding reduces aqueous solubility relative to polar donors.

skills.hypothesis: Polar hydrogen-bond donors plus compact surface raise solubility, so donor-rich, compact molecules should score highest. Fails if polarity is offset by large hydrophobic surface.

rules.rationale: Ring-rich topology often means rigid, hydrophobic structure, lowering aqueous solubility.
High rotatability usually indicates flexible, non-planar hydrophobic surface, reducing solubility.
Counterintuitively, donor-free apolar molecules can be highly soluble if small and compact.
Very long SMILES encodes huge molecules, which are almost always insoluble.

skills.hypothesis: Ring-rich, flexible hydrophobic topology lowers solubility, so the donor-rich prior may be reversed. Fails if ring-rich molecules are small and polar.

lesson: Across four seeds, donor-rich and donor-mid candidates scored highest, while rings_high and smiles_very_long candidates scored lowest, confirming the polar-donor mechanism and the weakness of ring/rotatable priors. Compact surface (smiles_short) lifted scores, so adding that reward refines the winning skill.
revision_summary: Retained the deployed donor-rich skill and replaced the long_smiles penalty with a compact_surface reward, keeping the same ridge, semantic mass, and UCB settings. Kept the ring/rotatable counter-hypothesis unchanged. Deployed the refined donor-plus-compact skill because its strongest observed candidates matched donor_mid plus rings_none, and its weakest candidates were ring_rich plus smiles_very_long, consistent with the mechanistic solubility mechanism.
